prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1361; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a report of a low-speed collision in a parking lot. Claimant reports being struck while exiting a parking space. Claimant states a wrist injury occurred during the incident and that they have sought initial medical care. No attorney representation noted at intake. Claimant asked for the process to be explained and was provided the general steps for filing a bodily injury component.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant describes pain and swelling in the left wrist and reports a diagnosis of a fracture from urgent care. Requested copies of the medical records and an itemized bill. Claimant indicated they are not working with a lawyer and prefers to handle communication directly. Advised claimant of their right to seek legal counsel at any time.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos submitted by claimant showing vehicle damage to the rear quarter panel and a cracked taillight on the claimant's vehicle. Parking lot surveillance was requested from the property owner, with a note that footage may be overwritten on a rolling schedule. Witness statement form sent to the claimant for any bystanders identified.

Entry 4: Received medical records from the treating provider. Records confirm a fracture of the distal radius with a splint applied and follow-up with an orthopedic specialist scheduled. Claimant reports ongoing limited grip strength and difficulty with daily tasks. Noted that treatment is ongoing, so the injury evaluation remains open pending the specialist's findings.

Entry 5: Contacted the other driver's insurer to confirm coverage and liability position. Insurer acknowledged the report and stated liability is under review based on the parking lot footage and statements. Claimant updated on status and reminded to forward any new bills or treatment notes. File remains open for injury evaluation and property damage estimate.
